_about: Every definition the site shows (scripts/definitions.py). Edited in the admin’s Definitions tab; only status "live" text reaches the site.

direction.Fade: Fade means bet the other side.

last_time_format.side: Last time: {date}, {team} was {price} vs {opp}. {winner} won the {segment} {score}.
last_time_format.note: {result} is the plain outcome of the bet, e.g. 'Over 1.5', 'both teams scored', 'tied'. Never a ✓ or ✗.

record_line.tooltip: Record betting this trend this season, how often it won, how often the same bet won across all games, and profit at 1 unit per bet.

streaks.section: Teams on a run of 3 or more straight in the opening segment, counted from their most recent game. A tie or push ends a streak.
streaks.colors: Win and loss streaks run green to red. Over/Under and Yes/No streaks get darker the longer they run.

config.lean_rule: A team's lean = 60%+ of its games, 5+ played.

term:3-way-moneyline.name: 3-Way Moneyline
term:3-way-moneyline.short: Common in soccer betting, except here the draw is called a tie: Team A, Team B or Tie. If it ends level, Team A and Team B both lose. That's why the prices are better.

term:btts.name: Both Teams to Score (BTTS)
term:btts.short: Yes means both teams score in the segment; No means at least one gets shut out. In NHL first periods, BTTS Yes has hit 36% this season, which is why it pays plus money.

term:first-five.name: First Five (F5)
term:first-five.short: Baseball bets that settle after five innings: moneyline, run line and total. You're betting the starting pitchers, not the bullpens.

term:league-average.name: League average
term:league-average.short: What a side hits across the whole league. If home teams win the 1P 51% of the time, a team at 51% is just average.

term:moneyline.name: Moneyline (ML)
term:moneyline.short: Pick who wins the segment. That's it. In the 2-way version, a tie is a push and you get your money back.

term:nrfi.name: NRFI / YRFI
term:nrfi.short: No Run First Inning / Yes Run First Inning. NRFI wins if nobody scores in the 1st, YRFI if anybody does. It came in 49.4% NRFI in 2026, basically a coin flip, so the price is everything.

term:push.name: Push
term:push.short: A tie against the number: you get your money back. A 2-way moneyline pushes on a tied segment, and a whole-number spread or total can land right on it.

term:run-line.name: Run Line
term:run-line.short: Baseball's spread. In the first five it's most often 1/2 a run, so a tie after five goes to the underdog.

term:spread.name: Spread (ATS)
term:spread.short: The favorite has to win by more than the number; the underdog can lose by less and still cash. In the first quarter you'll most often see 1/2 to 1 point.

term:total.name: Total (Over/Under, O/U)
term:total.short: Bet on the combined score going over or under the number. NHL first periods are almost always 1.5: get two goals and you've got a winner.

term:units.name: Units (u)
term:units.short: How we keep score in money terms: 1 unit risked on every game at the closing price. +6.4u means you'd be up 6.4 times your bet size. A dash means we don't have enough prices saved for that team yet.

term:team-total.name: Team Total
term:team-total.short: Over/under on one team's score only.

term:side.name: Side
term:side.short: Which team you're on: home or away, favorite or underdog.

term:first-segment-bet.name: First-segment bet
term:first-segment-bet.short: A bet on just the start of the game: the first period, quarter, half, inning or five innings. It settles fast, and you're not sweating the fourth quarter.

term:1st-period.name: 1st Period (1P)
term:1st-period.short: The first 20 minutes of an NHL game. It settles in about 35-40 minutes. The most common 1st period score this season: 1-0.

term:1st-quarter.name: 1st Quarter (1Q)
term:1st-quarter.short: The first 12 minutes (NBA), 10 (WNBA) or 15 (NFL, college football). Books price an NBA first quarter a point or two above a straight quarter of the total.

term:1st-half.name: 1st Half (1H)
term:1st-half.short: Everything up to halftime. Overtime never counts. College basketball first halves are priced a few points under half the game total.

term:1st-inning.name: 1st Inning
term:1st-inning.short: The top and bottom of the 1st. That's where NRFI and YRFI live.

term:tie.name: Tie
term:tie.short: The segment ends level. On a 2-way moneyline that's a push; on the 3-way, only the tie bet wins. NHL first periods have ended tied 34% of the time this season, and about half of those were 1-1.

term:half-point.name: Half-point (hook)
term:half-point.short: The .5 on a line. It means no push is possible: somebody wins, somebody loses.

term:american-odds.name: American odds
term:american-odds.short: Minus is the favorite: -150 means bet $150 to win $100. Plus is the underdog: +150 means bet $100 to win $150.

term:favorite.name: Favorite
term:favorite.short: The team the book expects to win. You pay more to back it (a minus price).

term:underdog.name: Underdog
term:underdog.short: The team the book expects to lose. You get paid more if it wins (a plus price).

term:juice.name: Juice (vig)
term:juice.short: The book's cut, built into the price. That's why both sides of a spread are -110, not even money.

term:best-price.name: Best price
term:best-price.short: The best odds on a side across the books we track, outlined in green. Same bet, more money back.

term:opening-line.name: Opening line
term:opening-line.short: The first price a book posts.

term:closing-line.name: Closing line
term:closing-line.short: The last price before the game starts. Every Run To Your Bets record and unit is graded at the closing line.

term:line-move.name: Line move
term:line-move.short: How far a price moved from open to now. A big move often means money came in on one side.

term:record.name: Record
term:record.short: Wins, losses and ties (or pushes), always shown with the % first: 80% (12-3-8). The header tells you which sides: W-L-T, O-U, Y-N.

term:win.name: Win %
term:win.short: Wins divided by wins plus losses. Ties and pushes are left out, except on the 3-way, where a tie counts as a loss.

term:trend.name: Trend
term:trend.short: A situation and how it's done this season, like "fade teams off a loss: 57% (150-111)." Graded every night.

term:league-trend.name: League trend
term:league-trend.short: A trend across the whole league, shown with the league average next to it so you can see if it's real or just noise.

term:streak.name: Streak
term:streak.short: How many games in a row a team has hit the same result in a market, like "1Q Under · 11 straight." A push or tie ends it.

term:last-10.name: Last 10 (L10)
term:last-10.short: A team's record over its last 10 games in that market. Hot or cold right now, not all season.

term:split.name: Split
term:split.short: A team's record in one situation: home, away, favorite, back-to-back, after a loss.

term:rest.name: Rest
term:rest.short: Days off before the game. 0 days means a back-to-back.

term:edge.name: Edge
term:edge.short: When our numbers say a side wins more often than its price says it should. That gap is the edge.

label:dumpster_fire.name: 🗑️🔥 Dumpster Fire
label:dumpster_fire.short: Both teams have lost the {segment} (moneyline) or failed to cover it (spread) in 60%+ of their games (5+ played).
